correctness.rationale: After eliminating the nonzero peripheral diagonal coordinates, the shifted clique block is uniformly symmetric. Normalize the rank-t surviving coupling to I_t plus zeros. The paired block [[U,I],[I,0]] is nonsingular and its inverse has zero clique-to-clique block, so eliminating it leaves the original symmetric restriction on the k−t uncoupled clique directions. This is the needed fact even in characteristic two; no alternating bilinear form is assumed. Rectangular factorization modulo GL_t gives the rank count. Choosing the radical and then an invertible quotient form gives the symmetric rank count. In particular, bordering gives h_d=(1−1/q)h_(d−1)+q^(−1)(1−q^(−(d−1)))h_(d−2) with h_0=1 and h_1=1−1/q: only old radicals of dimension zero or one can contribute to nonsingularity. With dimension one the new column must pair nontrivially with the radical. The recurrence yields the odd-factor product. Nonsingularity then forces s=t and a nonsingular residual form. For critical scaling the difference from (S_m−k)_+ is twice the rectangular defect plus the residual symmetric corank. The first is uniformly tight by a kernel-subspace union bound, the second by the expected number (<1) of nonzero nullvectors, since each fixed nonzero vector can be made the first basis vector and the corresponding column is uniform. The CLT and Slutsky apply. An m^(1/4) band about k has o(1) probability at critical scale, while on S_m<k−m^(1/4) the two rank factors converge uniformly to 1 and h_∞; the strict sides follow by binomial concentration. Independently, python /workspace/reproductions/nullity.py matched the complete spectra for five additional (q,k,m) triples over prime fields by counting kernel vectors, not by replaying uploaded code. This is bounded corroboration, not the all-field or asymptotic proof.
